problem.title: Benefits Enrollment Gated by Onboarding Status
problem.prompt: You are working with an HR platform tracking onboarding completion and benefits enrollment, modeled on public workforce datasets (BLS, Census). The `employees` table records each employee's department code (NAICS 2-digit), onboarding completion flag stored as a text value ('Y' or 'N'), and hire date. The `benefit_plans` table records all plan options an employee can choose from, with monthly premium amounts and plan types stored as an array of tags. Some employees have multiple plan options; others may have none listed yet. Write a query that returns one row per employee showing their employee_id, department (cleaned and capitalized), hire_month name (no padding), and their lowest available monthly premium IF they have completed onboarding (onboarding_complete = 'Y'), otherwise 0. If an employee has no plans listed, treat their premium as NULL before applying the gate. Exclude any employee hired on or after 2024-07-01. Order by employee_id ascending.

display.context: You are working with an HR platform tracking onboarding completion and benefits enrollment, modeled on public workforce datasets (BLS, Census).
display.task: Write a query that returns each employee's ID, department, hire month name, and their lowest available monthly premium if they completed onboarding, otherwise 0.

table_notes.employees: records each employee's department code, onboarding completion flag (stored as text 'Y' or 'N'), and hire date
table_notes.benefit_plans: records all plan options available to each employee with monthly premium amounts and plan type tags

output_field_notes.employee_id: the unique identifier for the employee
output_field_notes.department: the department name cleaned of whitespace and with each word capitalized
output_field_notes.hire_month: the name of the month the employee was hired with no trailing padding
output_field_notes.lowest_premium: the smallest monthly premium among the employee's available plans if they completed onboarding, otherwise zero; null if no plans are listed

field_logic: department: take the department name from the employees table, remove spaces around it, and capitalize each word
hire_month: extract the month name from the hire date with no trailing spaces

lowest_premium: find the smallest monthly premium value across all of the employee's benefit plan rows; if the employee's onboarding completion flag is 'Y' use that minimum, otherwise use 0; if the employee has no plan rows the minimum is null and the gate still applies (null if completed, 0 if not)
edge_cases: If an employee has multiple benefit plan rows, pick the one with the smallest monthly premium.
If an employee has completed onboarding (the text value 'Y') and has at least one plan, output the lowest premium.
If an employee has not completed onboarding (the text value is not 'Y'), output 0 for the premium.
If an employee has no benefit plan rows at all, the minimum is null before the gate is applied.
display.filter_note: Only employees hired before 2024-07-01 are included.
display.order_by_note: Rows are ordered by employee_id ascending.

composite_moves: look up onboarding_complete gate from employees
per-entity pick: MIN(monthly_premium) from benefit_plans per employee_id
gate with CASE: if onboarding_complete::boolean then min_premium else 0
clean department_name with TRIM and INITCAP
extract hire_month with TO_CHAR using FM modifier
handle NULL min_premium with COALESCE in CASE
round final premium to two decimals

hints: Start by joining employees and benefit_plans, then think about how to get one premium per employee.
You'll need to find the minimum premium for each employee, but only use it if a certain condition is met on the employees table.

Use a LEFT JOIN with the gate condition in the ON clause so non-qualifiers are preserved with NULL premiums, then apply a CASE to substitute 0 when the gate fails or the premium is NULL; remember to cast the text onboarding flag to boolean, clean the department name, and extract the month name without padding.
problem.answer_key: SELECT e.employee_id, INITCAP(TRIM(e.department_name)) AS department, TO_CHAR(e.hire_date, 'FMMonth') AS hire_month, ROUND(CASE WHEN e.onboarding_complete::boolean THEN COALESCE(bp_min.min_premium, 0) ELSE 0 END, 2) AS lowest_premium FROM employees e LEFT JOIN (SELECT employee_id, MIN(monthly_premium) AS min_premium FROM benefit_plans GROUP BY employee_id) bp_min ON e.employee_id = bp_min.employee_id WHERE e.hire_date < DATE '2024-07-01' ORDER BY e.employee_id;

_meta.scenario: an HR platform tracking onboarding completion and benefits enrollment

user_solution:
/*
*/
SELECT
    e.employee_id,
    INITCAP(TRIM(e.department_name)) AS department,
    TO_CHAR(e.hire_date, 'FMMonth') AS hire_month,
    ROUND(MIN(CASE WHEN b.plan_id IS NULL THEN NULL
         WHEN onboarding_complete = 'Y' THEN b.monthly_premium ELSE 0 END),2) AS lowest_premium
FROM employees AS e
LEFT JOIN benefit_plans AS b
    ON e.employee_id = b.employee_id
WHERE e.hire_date::date < '2024-07-01'
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
ORDER BY e.employee_id;
